entries.text: Busybodies exhorted to mind their own business.

text.text: For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies.
Now them that are such we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread.
He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.

entries.text: Christians exhorted not to suffer as a consequence of being a meddler in other people's matters.

text.text: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.

entries.text: We are not to wander from house to house as tattlers and busybodies.

text.text: And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.

entries.text: We should not meddle in other's concerns.

text.text: Thou hast indeed smitten Edom, and thine heart hath lifted thee up: glory of this, and tarry at home: for why shouldest thou meddle to thy hurt, that thou shouldest fall, even thou, and Judah with thee?
It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.
My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change:
He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.

entries.text: Gossiping is not proper and a sign of a depraved mind.

text.text: And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;
Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,
It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.

entries.text: We are admonished not to gossip.

text.text: For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found unto you such as ye would not: lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults:

entries.text: We should not talk about the errors or transgressions of others.

text.text: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.
All that hate me whisper together against me: against me do they devise my hurt.

entries.text: Gossip causes a separation in friendship.

text.text: A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends.
He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.

entries.text: Do not associate with a gossip.

text.text: He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.

entries.text: Where gossiping is eliminated, strife ceases.

text.text: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
